image.subject: a candle-lit 18th-century lodge room at night, a long wooden table with a single sealed letter, empty chairs pulled back, a closed door in the shadows

storyboard.claim: Joining the order meant giving up your life to an invisible hierarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dim lodge room with one candle and an empty table, no people, so the secrecy is what the viewer sees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Picks up the oath from the previous beat and turns it into the setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lodge as a physical room of secrecy.

image.subject: a candle-lit 18th-century library at night, a wooden table piled with books and a handwritten manifesto, no one in the room

storyboard.claim: The order's aim was to overthrow superstition and monarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A manifesto on a desk in a library, showing the plan on paper.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the lodge oath to the goal the oath served.
storyboard.addedInformation: The plan was written down, not only whispered.

image.subject: an 18th-century Bavarian university lecture hall at dusk, rows of empty wooden benches under a tall window of pale light

storyboard.claim: The group called itself the Illuminati and drew on the Enlightenment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A university hall at dusk, the setting where the reason-based ideas were taught.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the plan to the intellectual source of the name.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Illuminati came out of university teaching.

image.subject: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, standing at a tall window and looking down at a market square

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt wanted to unite humanity as one family without princes, nations or churches.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt at a window, looking down on the town, the founder's vision of the world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the founder as the person behind the plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: His ambition was global, not local.

image.subject: a crowded 18th-century Bavarian town square at midday, a Catholic church spire and a royal palace rising behind the rooftops

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt was a radical Enlightenment thinker living in a conservative Catholic state.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The church spire and palace over the square, the conservative power he lived under.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the danger in the founder's situation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Bavaria was dominated by church and crown.

storyboard.claim: To spread a dangerous idea you need a plan for surviving the spread.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bare question card on the screen with no picture, so the question stands alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the problem of spreading a dangerous idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beats as an engineering question.

image.subject: a sealed letter pushed under the heavy wooden door of a stone house on a dark 18th-century street at night

storyboard.claim: Ideas aimed at overthrowing the monarchy and church must travel in secret.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A letter slipped under a door at night, showing covert transmission.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question with the method: secret delivery.
storyboard.addedInformation: Covert letters were the medium of the danger.

image.subject: an empty 18th-century European town square at dusk, wet cobblestones, a locked city gate and a single lantern, no people

storyboard.claim: You cannot shout a dangerous idea in a public square; the state would silence you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty square at dusk, with no people, showing the public place that is closed to such ideas.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the open route is impossible.
storyboard.addedInformation: The square is the place power watches.

image.subject: a folded letter with a red wax seal on a worn wooden table beside a lit candle, a small cipher key lying next to it

storyboard.claim: The idea must move through an encrypted, decentralised network to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wax-sealed letter and cipher key, the tools of a hidden network.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the method that the square-and-state problem demanded.
storyboard.addedInformation: Secrecy was built with letters and codes.

storyboard.claim: The network began very small.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bare question card, no picture, to let the pause land.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the encrypted network with a question about its size.
storyboard.addedInformation: Prompts the viewer to expect a small number.

storyboard.claim: By December 1779 the Illuminati had only 60 members, confined to a few Bavarian university towns.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Large numeral 60 with the date, no picture needed for a number.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the small-start question with the figure.
storyboard.addedInformation: The date and the university-town base.

image.subject: a hand-drawn 18th-century map of southern German lands with fine ink lines linking a few university towns

storyboard.claim: A tiny clique in a few Bavarian towns became a global bogeyman.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A hand-drawn map with ink lines linking the towns, showing the small base.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the number to the geography of the network.
storyboard.addedInformation: The map shows where the network sat.

image.subject: a stone bridge over a river at dusk with a single courier on horseback crossing toward the far bank

storyboard.claim: Weak ties and network contagion made the Illuminati's growth explode.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A courier crossing a bridge, the link between two separate places.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the mechanism behind the map's connections.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the bridge metaphor used later.

storyboard.claim: By the early 1780s the Illuminati had roughly 1300 members.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Large numeral 1300 with the date, a plain figure card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the growth the contagion produced.
storyboard.addedInformation: The jump from 60 to about 1300.

image.subject: an 18th-century palace salon at night, gilded mirrors and candles, gentlemen in dark frock coats talking in pairs

storyboard.claim: The members were now infiltrating the ranks of the elite.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A palace salon of men in frock coats, the elite spaces the network entered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the growth with the social level it reached.
storyboard.addedInformation: Students became courtiers and officials.

image.subject: the host Niall Ferguson, a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books

storyboard.claim: Weak ties matter for understanding how everyday life works.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his desk, speaking directly to the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host steps in to slow down and explain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Addresses the viewer personally.

storyboard.claim: Your closest friends share your news, people and places, so you live in a bubble.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three items listed as text, the shared traits of a close circle.
storyboard.onScreenText: SAME NEWS / SAME FRIENDS / SAME PLACES
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the everyday example of the bubble.
storyboard.addedInformation: Three traits that keep a close circle closed.

image.subject: an 18th-century coffee-house counter in a Bavarian town, a waiter and a customer exchanging a few words over a cup

storyboard.claim: A weak tie is an acquaintance you see only now and then, who connects you to a new circle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A brief exchange across a coffee-house counter, a casual link between strangers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the bubble a bridge: the casual acquaintance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The weak tie is casual, not a close friend.

left.label: CLOSE CIRCLE
left.subject: a tight group of four friends around a candle-lit table in an 18th-century room

right.label: WEAK TIE
right.subject: two acquaintances meeting briefly on a cobbled street corner

storyboard.claim: A weak tie links you to a different cluster of people, while close friends keep you inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two side-by-side pictures: a closed group against a brief street meeting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the barista example into a clear contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: Close friends stay in one cluster; weak ties reach others.

image.subject: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, seated at a desk with two open letters side by side

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt used weak ties to jump between social clusters rather than recruiting only friends.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt at his desk with two letters, one for each cluster he reached.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the weak-tie idea to the founder.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two letters show two separate circles being connected.

storyboard.claim: The sociologist Mark Granovetter wrote a famous paper on weak ties in the 1970s.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A document card titled The Strength of Weak Ties, no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the source of the idea.
storyboard.addedInformation: The 1970s sociologist and his paper title.

image.subject: a stone bridge joining two town districts at dusk, a crowd crossing in both directions over the water

storyboard.claim: Ideas spread across the bridges between communities, not inside tight families.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bridge with people crossing both ways, the flow between communities.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the bridge image to the general principle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ideas travel between groups, not within them.

image.subject: an 18th-century courier in a dark travelling cloak standing at the doorway of a lodge, a sealed letter in hand

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt used weak ties to move from the students into the broader Freemason networks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A courier at a lodge doorway, the link between the students and the older order.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the next jump in the network, from students to Freemasons.
storyboard.addedInformation: The courier carries the connection.

image.subject: a candle-lit lodge room, a wooden table with a square and compass and an open rulebook, two chairs drawn up

storyboard.claim: The students were brought into the established Freemason lodges.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lodge table with a square and compass and rulebook.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the destination of the courier's connection.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lodge's tools and rulebook.

storyboard.claim: Through the enlightenment salons they recruited a literary giant and the Duke of Saxe-Weimar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card; the names are spoken, and no portrait is authored for these figures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the lodge network into the salons.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the Weimar court as a recruit.

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt understood viral networks centuries before the internet existed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timeline card with the 18th century on one end and the internet on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the network point across time.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the idea in a long historical line.

image.subject: an 18th-century library with tall shelves of ledgers and books, a single candle on a long table, a folded map unrolled across it

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt sounds like an evil genius architect of society.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A library table with a map and candle, the planning room of a mastermind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the image of the mastermind the narration seems to describe.
storyboard.addedInformation: The map and ledgers suggest planning.

storyboard.claim: His private letters show the reality is funnier and less sinister.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bare question card, no picture, to set up the reveal.
storyboard.onScreenText: BUT WHAT DO THE LETTERS SAY?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the mastermind image toward the letters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Points to the private letters as evidence.

image.subject: a wooden desk with an empty brass cipher wheel, a half-written letter and an unlit candle, no one at the desk

storyboard.claim: The encrypted machine was a bluff; the machine did not exist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty cipher wheel and unfinished letter, the machine is only a prop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the machine question with the bluff.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cipher machine was never built.

storyboard.claim: He designed the idea of a machine, not the machine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Punchline card with no picture, the reveal lands in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the bluff with the reversal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only the idea existed.

storyboard.claim: Weishaupt told a new recruit the ancient order only existed in his mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quotation card reading that the order only existed in his mind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the confession that backs the bluff.
storyboard.addedInformation: The founder's own words, to a recruit.

image.subject: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, sitting alone at an empty desk in a dim study with one candle

storyboard.claim: There was no ancient architecture of the order; he faked it until it became real.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt alone at an empty desk, the order existed only in his head.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the confession with the image of the lonely founder.
storyboard.addedInformation: No ancient structure stood behind the order.

image.subject: two gentlemen in an 18th-century salon examining a folded document as if it were a treasure, candles lit on the wall behind them

storyboard.claim: He sold bored intellectuals the story of a massive ancient conspiracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men absorbed in a document, the intellectuals taking the story in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the audience that bought the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: The recruits were bored intellectuals.

storyboard.claim: The belief in the story is what built the network.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Plain statement card, a beat of banter with no picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A reaction beat that closes the bluff.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the belief back to the building of the network.

image.subject: a single candle burning in a dark lodge room, its light falling on an empty chair and a closed book

storyboard.claim: The order was made real through confidence alone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone candle in a dark lodge, belief as the only light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the bluff in one image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Confidence as the source of the network's power.

image.subject: a stone royal palace tower looming over a crowded cobbled town square at dusk, a narrow dark passage running beneath the square

storyboard.claim: The bluff worked as a hidden square running beneath the monarchical tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tower above, a hidden passage below the square, the square-and-tower image of the book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the book's central metaphor for the bluff.
storyboard.addedInformation: Power above, network below.

image.subject: a courier in a dark cloak slipping a folded letter to a man in a doorway on a cobbled street at dusk, two uniformed police officers walking past without looking

storyboard.claim: The network bypassed government sensors and the state police while moving ideas fast.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A letter passed in plain sight while officers walk on, the network slipping past the state.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the tower's blindness to the hidden square.
storyboard.addedInformation: The state police are present and unaware.

image.subject: a crowded 18th-century German tavern at night, men leaning over tables talking over tankards of beer

storyboard.claim: To change society the network had to move from pub talk to real power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tavern full of men talking, the stage where ideas start.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the hidden network to the question of using it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tavern as the starting point of ideas.

image.subject: a candle-lit lodge room at night, a map spread across the table and a knot of men in dark coats leaning over it

storyboard.claim: The network had to undergo a fundamental paradoxical mutation to wield power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Men gathered over a map, the group that is about to change shape.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the turn the narration promises.
storyboard.addedInformation: The group must change shape to act.

image.subject: the host Niall Ferguson, a British historian in his fifties, short greying hair, dark sport jacket over an open-collar shirt, seated at a wooden desk with books

storyboard.claim: Networks show how they behave when they meet existing power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host at his desk, returning to the lesson for the viewer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk by returning to the host to frame the lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lesson is about how networks meet existing power.
